### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications across the three files work together to address a use-after-free issue encountered during the destruction of a QP. 

- The addition of the `qp_free` completion structure in `siw.h` allows for synchronization between the QP destruction process and the reference counting mechanism.
- The initialization of this completion structure in `siw_verbs.c` ensures that the QP destroy function can wait for all references to be dropped before it returns.
- Finally, the signaling of the completion in `siw_qp.c` indicates that it is safe to free the QP, thus preventing any potential use-after-free scenarios that could occur if the QP were accessed after it had been freed. 

Overall, these changes ensure that the QP destruction process is properly synchronized with reference counting, thereby enhancing the stability and reliability of the RDMA/siw implementation.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by a use-after-free condition where the `siw_cm_work_handler` was referencing a QP that had already been freed after a QP destroy call. This occurred because the QP destroy process did not wait for all references to the QP to be dropped before completing the destruction, leading to potential access of invalid memory.
        
        Commit message:
        RDMA/siw: Fix QP destroy to wait for all references dropped.

Delay QP destroy completion until all siw references to QP are
dropped. The calling RDMA core will free QP structure after
successful return from siw_qp_destroy() call, so siw must not
hold any remaining reference to the QP upon return.
A use-after-free was encountered in xfstest generic/460, while
testing NFSoRDMA. Here, after a TCP connection drop by peer,
the triggered siw_cm_work_handler got delayed until after
QP destroy call, referencing a QP which has already freed.

Fixes: 303ae1cdfdf7 ("rdma/siw: application interface")
Reported-by: Olga Kornievskaia <kolga@netapp.com>
Signed-off-by: Bernard Metzler <bmt@zurich.ibm.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220920082503.224189-1-bmt@zurich.ibm.com
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leon@kernel.org>  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/sw/siw/siw_verbs.c b/drivers/infiniband/sw/siw/siw_verbs.c
index 8dedae7ae79e..3e814cfb298c 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/sw/siw/siw_verbs.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/sw/siw/siw_verbs.c
@@ -480,6 +480,8 @@ int siw_create_qp(struct ib_qp *ibqp, struct ib_qp_init_attr *attrs,
 	list_add_tail(&qp->devq, &sdev->qp_list);
 	spin_unlock_irqrestore(&sdev->lock, flags);
 
+	init_completion(&qp->qp_free);
+
 	return 0;
 
 err_out_xa:
@@ -624,6 +626,7 @@ int siw_destroy_qp(struct ib_qp *base_qp, struct ib_udata *udata)
 	qp->scq = qp->rcq = NULL;
 
 	siw_qp_put(qp);
+	wait_for_completion(&qp->qp_free);
 
 	return 0;
 }
--

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
qp->attrs.flags |= SIW_QP_IN_DESTROY;
siw_qp_put(qp);
```
Reason:
The `siw_qp_put(qp)` call decreases the reference count of the QP, potentially freeing it while the `siw_cm_work_handler` could still be referencing it. This leads to a use-after-free condition if the handler accesses the QP after it has been freed.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
wait_for_completion(&qp->qp_free);
init_completion(&qp->qp_free);
```
Reason:
The addition of `wait_for_completion(&qp->qp_free);` ensures that the QP destroy process waits until all references to the QP are dropped before completing the destruction. The `init_completion(&qp->qp_free);` initializes a completion structure that allows the destroy function to block until it is safe to proceed, preventing access to a freed QP.
